findings.title: Group resources created without type, breaking findByType lookup
findings.body: When creating a resource for a specific group via getOrCreateResource(), the code does not call resource.setType(resourceType). The all-groups type-level resource created in init() does have its type set, but individual group resources do not. As a result, GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() uses resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) and will not find these resources, causing the method to always return an empty set. This breaks pre-filtering of users by group membership in UsersResource.searchForUser() and, more importantly, leads to incorrect user counts in UsersResource.getUsersCount(), as the storage query will count all users instead of only those in groups the admin can view.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns resource UUIDs instead of Keycloak group IDs
findings.body: In the lambda for resourceStore.findByType, the code adds groupResource.getId() to the granted set. However, groupResource.getId() is the internal authorization resource UUID, not the Keycloak group ID. The set is later used as a filter for user search via session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds), which expects actual group IDs. Since the resource name is set to the group ID (in AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup), the correct value is groupResource.getName(). This bug causes user filtering by group membership to fail and, when combined with missing type on group resources, completely breaks group-based user search and count.

findings.title: canManage() incorrectly grants manage permission for VIEW scope
findings.body: The method canManage() returns hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE). This means an admin with only the VIEW scope on the all-groups resource is considered to have global manage permission for groups. As a result, such an admin could call requireManage() and perform operations like creating top-level groups or other manage-level actions, violating the intended authorization model. The check should only include AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE, not VIEW.

findings.title: Potential NullPointerException when all-groups resource is missing
findings.body: In hasPermission(), if groupId is null and the all-groups resource cannot be found (e.g., admin permissions schema not initialized or resource type resource not created), getResourceTypeResource() returns null. The subsequent call policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) will throw a NullPointerException instead of returning false. This could lead to HTTP 500 errors for unauthorized access attempts. The code should check if resource is null before calling findByResource.
